e-5490.knowledge_point: Calculating the Components of an Eigenvector Corresponding to a Given Eigenvalue
e-5490.problem:
The vector $\mathbf{v}$ and the matrix $A$ are given below. 
If $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda=3,$ then what is the value of $\dfrac{b}{c}?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069621/assets/5f1bfa33d135d95e3153e3305da50b69541d88d1cd78b5b6ad030a89861f3e10.png)
e-5490.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & -6 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -6 \\ 2 & -2 & -4 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-6{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -6 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & -4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & -4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, $x_3$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain $x_2=x_3.$ From the first equation, we get $x_1=3x_3.$ Therefore, the general solution is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069621/assets/f2707b01c13749362887e4ae0da130466ae753dccd4bc354600af79f71c3de5f.png)

Setting, for instance, $x_3=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069621/assets/8e7627a6a515086ff53f5ed250a070e08ee2b71d0e4fb3d79e5434218d028624.png)

Finally, $\dfrac{b}{c}=\dfrac{1}{1}=1.$

Find an eigenvector of

that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda=-2.$
e-5491.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, $x_2$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain $x_3=0.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get $x_1=-x_2.$ Therefore, the general solution is

Setting, for instance, $x_2=1,$ we get the eigenvector

e-5492.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvectors of a 3x3 Matrix
e-5492.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069621/assets/1503285c91d0c320a3720c702b620bfe2156ed713d915b04c22bd35c06a05cd8.png)

The vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1=1$ and $\lambda_2=-1$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector $\mathbf{v}_3=\big[ a, \, b, \, c \big]^T$ such that the set $\{ \mathbf{v}_1,\mathbf{v}_2, \mathbf{v}_3 \}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\dfrac{a}{c}?$
e-5492.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is a diagonal matrix, we have that its eigenvalues are the entries in the main diagonal, that is, $\lambda_1=1,$ $\lambda_2=-1$ and $\lambda_3=4.$ 

Also, since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors $\{ \mathbf{v}_1,\mathbf{v}_2, \mathbf{v}_3 \},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ correspond to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1=1$ and $\lambda_2=-1.$ Thus, the third eigenvector $\mathbf{v}_3$ must correspond to $\lambda_3=4.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =4.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}=0 \\ -5{x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the augmented matrix $M$ is already in its row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In this matrix, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, $x_3$ is a free variable. From the first and second equations, we obtain $x_1=x_2=0.$  Therefore, the general solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069621/assets/7aab21fae627c5fe36b144f4a1e12a2d5e57ef7c2c987fbee64f718c7cbb7404.png)

Setting, for instance, $x_3=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069621/assets/c080641a794b7a65f7893429d32920f39bfb4d87d9193197afd6b48dacc697a3.png)

Finally, $\dfrac{a}{c}=\dfrac{0}{1}=0.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 9{x}_{1}-9{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 9 & -9 & -9 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-9){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & -27 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=(-\frac{1}{9}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]

If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3,$ then what is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & -6 & -9 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & -9 & -9 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 9{x}_{1}-9{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 9 & -9 & -9 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-9){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & -27 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=(-\frac{1}{9}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd one). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{3}.$ From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-3{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]

$$

$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =7,$ then what is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =7.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -9{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that its augmented matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{9}{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=9,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 9\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{3}{9}=\frac{1}{3}.$

decision.explanation: From (A-I)v=0, we have 20a-13b-9c=0 and 18a-12b-8c=0. Multiplying the first equation by 12 and subtracting 13 times the second gives 6a-4c=0. Thus a/c=2/3; c cannot be zero because that would force a=b=0.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}21 & -13 & -9 \\ 20 & -12 & -9 \\ 18 & -12 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1,$ then what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =1.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}21 & -13 & -9 \\ 20 & -12 & -9 \\ 18 & -12 & -7\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 \\ 20 & -13 & -9 \\ 18 & -12 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}20{x}_{1}-13{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ 20{x}_{1}-13{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ 18{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}-8{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 18 & -12 & -8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{9}{10}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10} & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{20}(13{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{20}(13(\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3})+9{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=3,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{2}{3}.$

$$

$$

\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 & -7 & 0 \\ 12 & -10 & 6 & 0 \\ 12 & -10 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -15 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -15 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -15 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=3{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{4}(-5{x}_{2}+7{x}_{3}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(-5(3{x}_{3})+7{x}_{3}) \\  & =2{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{2}{1}=2.$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-14 & 12 & 3 \\ -20 & 17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-14 & 12 & 3 \\ -20 & 17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 \\ -20 & 15 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-16{x}_{1}+12{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -20{x}_{1}+15{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 & 0 \\ -20 & 15 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{5}{4}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=4,$ we get the eigenvector

EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation (A−λI)x=0.

In our case, we have λ=2. So, we obtain

A−λI=[−14123−20174001]−2[100010001]=[−16123−2015400−1].

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

{−16x1+12x2+3x3=0−20x1+15x2+4x3=0−x3=0

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix M to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[−161230−20154000−10]R2:=R2+(−54)R1∼[−1612300014000−10]R3:=R3+4R2∼[−161230001400000]

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the 1st and the 3rd). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain x3=0. Substituting this in the first equation, we get x1=34x2. Therefore, the general solution is [34x2x20],x2∈R.

Setting, for instance, x2=4, we get the eigenvector v=[340].

content.knowledge_point: Calculating an Eigenvector Corresponding to a Given Eigenvalue
content.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-14 & 12 & 3 \\ -20 & 17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-14 & 12 & 3 \\ -20 & 17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 \\ -20 & 15 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-16{x}_{1}+12{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -20{x}_{1}+15{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 & 0 \\ -20 & 15 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{5}{4}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-16 & 12 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=4,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 13 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-9 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 13 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-11 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 11 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-11{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}-7{x}_{3}=0 \\ -14{x}_{1}+11{x}_{2}-8{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-11 & 9 & -7 & 0 \\ -14 & 11 & -8 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -14 & 11 & -8 & 0 \\ -11 & 9 & -7 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-7){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{11}{2}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -8 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{7}{2} & -7 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{7}{8}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=2{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation (A−λI)x=0.

In our case, we have λ=2. So, we obtain

A−λI=[−99−7−1413−8−212]−2[100010001]=[−119−7−1411−8−210].

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

{−11x1+9x2−7x3=0−14x1+11x2−8x3=0−2x1+x2=0

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix M to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[−119−70−1411−80−2100]R1↔R3∼[−2100−1411−80−119−70]R2:=R2+(−7)R1R3:=R3+(−112)R1∼[−210004−80072−70]R3:=R3+(−78)R2∼[−210004−800000]

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the 1st and the 2nd). Thus, x3 is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain x2=2x3. Substituting this in the first equation, we get x1=x3. Therefore, the general solution is [x32x3x3],x3∈R.

Setting, for instance, x3=1, we get the eigenvector v=[121].

content.knowledge_point: Calculating an Eigenvector Corresponding to a Given Eigenvalue
content.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 13 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-9 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 13 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-11 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 11 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-11{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}-7{x}_{3}=0 \\ -14{x}_{1}+11{x}_{2}-8{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-11 & 9 & -7 & 0 \\ -14 & 11 & -8 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -14 & 11 & -8 & 0 \\ -11 & 9 & -7 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-7){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{11}{2}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -8 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{7}{2} & -7 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{7}{8}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=2{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-3.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0 \\ 7{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-7){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}}{5} \\  & =\frac{-{x}_{2}+2(0)}{5} \\  & =-\frac{{x}_{2}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{{x}_{2}}{5} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

Question 8

Find an eigenvector of A=[21−20−31004] that corresponds to the eigenvalue λ=−3.

a
 [7−10]
b
 [−170]
c
 [−510]
d
[−150]
e
 [5−10]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation (A−λI)x=0.

In our case, we have λ=−3. So, we obtain

A−λI=[21−20−31004]−(−3)[100010001]=[51−2001007].

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

{5x1+x2−2x3=0x3=07x3=0

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix M to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[51−2000100070]R3:=R3+(−7)R2∼[51−2000100000]

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the 1st and the 3rd). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain x3=0. Substituting this into the first equation, we get x1=−x2+2x35=−x2+2(0)5=−x25. Therefore, the general solution is [−x25x20],x2∈R.

Setting, for instance, x2=5, we get the eigenvector v=[−150].

content.knowledge_point: Calculating an Eigenvector Corresponding to a Given Eigenvalue
content.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-3.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0 \\ 7{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-7){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}}{5} \\  & =\frac{-{x}_{2}+2(0)}{5} \\  & =-\frac{{x}_{2}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{{x}_{2}}{5} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Find an eigenvector of
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $2$nd and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{1}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{1}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

Find an eigenvector of A=[323011002] that corresponds to the eigenvalue λ=3.

EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation (A−λI)x=0.

In our case, we have λ=3. So, we obtain

A−λ=[323011002]−3[100010001]=[0230−2100−1].

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

{2x2+3x3=0−2x2+x3=0−x3=0

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix M to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[02300−21000−10]R2:=R2+R1∼[0230004000−10]R3:=R3+14R2∼[023000400000]

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the 2nd and the 3rd). Thus, x1 is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain x3=0. Substituting this into the first equation, we get x2=0. Therefore, the general solution is [x100],x1∈R.

Setting, for instance, x1=1, we get the eigenvector v=[100].

content.knowledge_point: Calculating an Eigenvector Corresponding to a Given Eigenvalue
content.problem:
Find an eigenvector of
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $2$nd and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{1}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{1}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-5{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-(\frac{1}{4}){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{2}:=(\frac{1}{4}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\  & ={x}_{2}+2(0) \\  & ={x}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating an Eigenvector Corresponding to a Given Eigenvalue
content.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-5{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-(\frac{1}{4}){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{2}:=(\frac{1}{4}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\  & ={x}_{2}+2(0) \\  & ={x}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find all the eigenvalues of $A$ by solving the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda  & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )((1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-(2)(2)) & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -3) & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)(\lambda +1)(\lambda -3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=3,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-2.$ Since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=-2.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{2}{3}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{20}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=4{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{3}(-2{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(-2(4{x}_{3})-4{x}_{3}) \\  & =-4{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{3} \\ 4{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{-4}{1}=-4.$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=3,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-2.$ Since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=-2.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.

In our case, we have $\lambda =-2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{2}{3}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{20}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=4{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{-4}{1}=-4.$

Question 13

A=[−40−43−3−3−402] The vectors v1 and v2 are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=4 and λ2=−3 of the matrix A, given above. Find the third eigenvector v3=[a,b,c]T such that the set {v1,v2,v3} is linearly independent. What is the value of ab?

a
−1
b
2
c
−2
d
12
e
−12
Submit

decision.explanation: The eigenvalues sum to tr(A)=-5, so the third eigenvalue is -5-4-(-3)=-6. Solving (A+6I)v₃=0 gives a=2c and a+b-c=0, hence b=-c. A nonzero solution requires c≠0, so a/b=-2.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-3$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find all the eigenvalues of $A$ by solving the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & -3-\lambda  & -3 \\ -4 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & -4 \\ -4 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-3-\lambda )((-4-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-(-4)(-4)) & =0 \\ (-3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda -24) & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)(\lambda +6)(\lambda -4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}=4,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-3,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-6.$ Since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-3.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=-6.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-6.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]-(-6)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & 3 & -3 \\ -4 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}+8{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & -3 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=-{x}_{3}.$ From the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{3}.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{2}{-1}=-2.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-3.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=-6.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$

$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-6.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]-(-6)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & 3 & -3 \\ -4 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

$$

$$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is an upper triangular matrix, we have that its eigenvalues are the entries in the main diagonal, that is, ${\lambda }_{1}=2,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=3.$ 

Also, since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=3.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -4{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the augmented matrix $M$ is already in its row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{5}{4}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\  & =4(\frac{5}{4}{x}_{3})-3{x}_{3} \\  & =5{x}_{3}-3{x}_{3} \\  & =2{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ \frac{5}{4}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=4,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{8}{4}=2.$

A=[−20−21−1−1−201] The vectors v1 and v2 are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=−3 and λ2=2 of the matrix A, given above. Find the third eigenvector v3=[a,b,c]T such that the set {v1,v2,v3} is linearly independent. What is the value of ab?

a
−1
b

c

decision.explanation: The eigenvalues sum to tr(A)=-2, so the third eigenvalue is -1. Solving (A+I)v₃=0 gives -a-2c=0 and a-c=0, forcing a=c=0. Thus b≠0 and a/b=0. Eigenvectors for the three distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find all the eigenvalues of $A$ by solving the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1-\lambda  & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-(-2)(-2)) & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -6) & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda +3)(\lambda -2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}=-3,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=2,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-1.$ Since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors ${{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=-1.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-1.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=0.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{0}{1}=0.$

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-1.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
